```{r}
#| label: setup
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)   # For ggplot, dplyr, and friends
library(moderndive)  # For rep_slice_sample() and un_member_states_2024
library(infer)       # For specify(), generate(), calculate(), and visualize()

# Load the Arab Barometer data
barometer <- read_csv("data/arab_barometer.csv")
```

## How many countries has a typical GU-Q student been to?

Replace these placeholder numbers with the numbers from the board:

```{r}
countries <- tibble(n_countries = c(1, 2, 3))
```

### Our estimate

```{r}
countries |>
  summarize(stat = median(n_countries))

ggplot(countries, aes(x = n_countries)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, color = "white")
```

### Lots of bootstraps

```{r}
set.seed(1234)
boot_countries <- countries |>
  rep_slice_sample(n = nrow(countries), replace = TRUE, reps = 1000) |>
  summarize(stat = median(n_countries))

ggplot(boot_countries, aes(x = stat)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, color = "white")
```

## The {infer} way

What's the median GDP per capita across countries? First, find the statistic from our actual data:

```{r}
#| warning: false

obs_median <- un_member_states_2024 |>
  specify(response = gdp_per_capita) |>
  calculate(stat = "median")

obs_median
```

Then make the bootstrap distribution and show where our statistic lands in it:

```{r}
#| warning: false

set.seed(1234)
boot_median <- un_member_states_2024 |>
  specify(response = gdp_per_capita) |>
  generate(reps = 1000, type = "bootstrap") |>
  calculate(stat = "median")

visualize(boot_median) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = obs_median$stat, linewidth = 1, color = "orange")
```
